advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Guard the review-bot voter's reviewbot-* clone path against a declared-but-unmounted scratch volume (mirror _require_scratch_volume), so the larger consumer also refuses instead of falling back to root.
evidence: voter.py:381 `with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix="reviewbot-") as repo_root:` — no dir= arg, so it follows TMPDIR/tempfile.gettempdir()
voter.py:379 `if not _review_clone_has_room(cfg):` is the only pre-clone gate; it does NOT call gate_admission/_require_scratch_volume

low_disk.py:69 `return has_min_free_space(tempfile.gettempdir())` — when the scratch volume is unmounted, gettempdir() is the empty root-resident mount-point dir, so this measures ROOT's free space and passes
search for `gate_admission(` shows only completion.py:338 and plan_review/__init__.py:278 call it — the voter never does
docker-compose.yml comment: TMPDIR clone is 'PER REVIEW … the larger of the two under load' — yet it is the consumer left unguarded by the refusal
advisory.finding: The declared-but-unmounted scratch-volume REFUSAL guards only the plan_review and verify_completion gates via gate_admission(); the review-bot voter's per-review reviewbot-* clone path is not guarded, so when the scratch volume is declared but unmounted the clone silently falls back to the root filesystem — the exact regression the story exists to prevent, for the consumer the change describes as the larger under load.
scenarios: Scratch volume declared (.gate-scratch-required present) but not mounted (proof absent); a review arrives and the voter clones reviewbot-* onto root while free space is ample, re-creating bug 3276's root-fill for the dominant consumer

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Make observability.sh gate the mounted heartbeat on the declaration marker the same way _require_scratch_volume does, so the probe's verdict matches the enforcement's in every marker combination.
evidence: observability.sh:173 `[ -f "$GATE_SCRATCH_MOUNT/.gate-scratch-mounted" ] && scratch_mounted=1` — no check of the declaration marker
gate_admission.py:171 `if not (base.parent / _SCRATCH_REQUIRED_MARKER).is_file(): return` — the refusal is opt-in by declaration, but the probe is not
observability.sh comment claims 'the probe and the refusal cannot disagree about the state of the same volume' — true only when a declaration exists
advisory.finding: observability.sh decides gate_scratch_mounted purely from the proof marker's presence, ignoring the declaration marker, whereas the refusal fires only when the declaration is ALSO present; on a host that has no declared scratch volume (no .gate-scratch-required) the probe would publish gate_scratch_mounted=0 and page rebar-gate-scratch-unmounted while gate admission does NOT refuse — monitoring and enforcement disagree in the neither-marker world.
scenarios: A Gerrit host provisioned before aa40 (or after an instance replacement that dropped the root-side declaration) runs observability.sh: proof marker absent, so gate_scratch_mounted=0 pages the unmounted alarm, but gates run normally because no declaration is present

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Make declaration-marker creation idempotent and automatic (e.g. write `.gate-scratch-required` in compose-up.sh when GATE_SCRATCH_MOUNT is configured, or a boot-time systemd unit) so the fail-closed guard cannot silently revert to OFF on instance replacement/re-image/restore.
evidence: user_data.sh:129 `touch "$GATE_SCRATCH_MOUNT/../.gate-scratch-required"` is the only writer of the declaration; gate_admission.py:171 returns (no refusal) when `_SCRATCH_REQUIRED_MARKER` is absent.
compose-up.sh:112-118 only `mkdir -p "$(dirname "${SCRATCH_MOUNT}")"` and emits a WARNING; it never creates `.gate-scratch-required`.

review-bot-ops.md new section: 'The DECLARATION is the one that is easy to lose without noticing: it is root-resident, so an instance replacement or a re-image drops it ... With it missing the guard is simply OFF — gates run ... right up until the volume goes away and they quietly go back to filling root.'
provision-restore.md step 4b requires the operator to manually recreate the markers in a specific order ('the declaration first, and the proof ONLY after mountpoint -q succeeds').
advisory.finding: The fail-closed guard's DECLARATION marker (`.gate-scratch-required`) is root-resident and is only written by `user_data.sh` at first boot; on instance replacement / re-image, or a restore that reuses an existing instance, it is lost while the guard silently reverts to OFF (gates run on root), and no automated step re-creates it — compose-up.sh only warns and never writes it.
scenarios: Instance replaced from a re-image / AMI refresh that does not re-run user_data mount steps; or a restore reusing an existing instance where /var/lib/rebar (root) was rebuilt without the declaration.
Operator recreates markers in the wrong order during recovery, landing the proof on root and reporting mounted-when-not.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Replace the source-text grep in test_the_probe_reads_the_same_marker_the_gate_refusal_reads with a behavioral assertion that drives observability.sh and checks the published gate_scratch_mounted value tracks the proof marker.
evidence: tests/scripts/test_observability_disk_pressure.py:346: code = "\n".join(line for line in SCRIPT.read_text().splitlines() if not line.lstrip().startswith("#"))
tests/scripts/test_observability_disk_pressure.py:349: assert ga._SCRATCH_MOUNTED_MARKER in code
tests/scripts/test_observability_disk_pressure.py:350: assert "mountpoint" not in code

SCRIPT is observability.sh, the script under test, driven behaviorally via _run() at line 139 — reading its source text as the assertion tests the implementation text, not behavior (Rule 4 litmus: renaming the shell var or adding a secondary mountpoint call breaks this with no behavior change).
advisory.finding: test_the_probe_reads_the_same_marker_the_gate_refusal_reads asserts on the TEXT of observability.sh (the source under test) rather than its behavior: it strips comments and checks `_SCRATCH_MOUNTED_MARKER in code` and `"mountpoint" not in code`. This is source-grepping / a change-detector — the forbid-token assertion (`"mountpoint" not in code`) breaks on any behavior-preserving refactor (e.g. adding mountpoint as a secondary settle check while still keying mountedness off the marker, or renaming a shell variable) with no observable-behavior change. The intended contract (probe and refusal agree because both read the same proof marker) is behaviorally testable by driving the script with a marker-present-but-mountpoint-would-disagree scenario, which the surrounding `_run`-based tests already demonstrate is feasible.
scenarios: A later edit adds `mountpoint -q` as a secondary settling/sanity check while still deriving the published value from the proof marker: behavior is unchanged but the test fails.
The shell variable/marker constant is renamed on both sides consistently: behavior unchanged, test fails.
advisory.suggested_fix: Drop the `"mountpoint" not in code` / `marker in code` text assertions; instead run the script (as the other §2e tests do) with the proof marker present vs absent and assert `gate_scratch_mounted` is 1 vs 0, demonstrating the metric keys off the same marker the refusal reads.

evidence: infra/compose/docker-compose.yml `- /var/lib/rebar:/var/lib/rebar` (bind of the parent directory)

gate_admission._require_scratch_volume returns (admits) when `.gate-scratch-required` is absent: src/rebar/llm/gate_admission.py:171 `if not (base.parent / _SCRATCH_REQUIRED_MARKER).is_file(): return`
docker-compose comment notes the review-bot image runs as root (line ~281 'The review-bot image runs as root, so the root-owned host dir is writable')
advisory.finding: The review-bot container binds the mount's PARENT `/var/lib/rebar:/var/lib/rebar`, which is root-resident and carries the `.gate-scratch-required` declaration marker; the container runs as root, so a compromised or buggy container process can delete that root-side marker and silently disarm the refusal guard (declaration-absent => admits, falling back to root).
